Can Viruses Change Our Genetic Code?

Many people wonder whether viruses can rewrite human DNA. The short answer is that viruses can insert some of their genetic material into our DNA, but they do not commonly modify our genetic code directly.

This insertion process is called integration. When it happens in humans, it is rare, and the inserted genetic material is usually inactive. That means it typically causes no genetic changes to the person.

So while viruses can leave genetic traces in our DNA, the idea that they routinely alter our genes is misleading. Integration can occur, but it does not mean our genetic code is being actively rewritten.
